Review Cal.com?

Reviewers mostly see Cal.com as a polished, easy scheduling tool with a clean interface, smooth setup, and strong calendar integrations, especially for Google and Microsoft users. Many say it feels better than Calendly, with useful customization, embedding, reminders, payments, and even built-in video. Technical users also value self-hosting and the open API; makers of IFTTT and Slashy specifically praise its flexibility and developer experience. The main complaints are uneven support, some Microsoft/Exchange connection gaps, and confusion over which features are truly open source.

### Where Cal.com Falls Short

 EU residency ends for most users. Cal.eu closes on 1 November 2026, per the shutdown notice dated 30 July 2026.
 Self-hosting lost team features. A September 2026 r/selfhosted thread on Calendly alternatives found Cal.diy polished but missing the team features the poster needed.
 Setup takes time. The March 2026 G2 review above called setup overwhelming and the docs unclear.
 Platform pricing. A 10-comment r/SaaS thread looked for a cheaper option than Cal.com Platform and found no clone that matched it.
 No native e-signatures. We found none in Cal.com's pricing, help center or changelog.

Cal.com Routing Forms Are Extremely Customizable

When we ran our integration/automation business, I cannot tell you HOW MANY REQUESTS we got for round robin scheduling. The problem at the time (pre-Cal.com days) was that round robin required a custom integration usually that was quite a kludgy and expensive solution (btw - despite Calendly being around since 2012, their round robin feature only came out in 2023 💀).

Cal.com is solving a HUGE need with round robin scheduling. If you have the need to cycle through calls to different team members and you want it to be done automatically, Cal.com is your best bet.

#### Weighted Round Robin [...] We personally use Motion (and even Superhuman Mail's scheduling feature) for our scheduling needs, however the caveat is that we really don't have many scheduling needs in our business (we have maybe 1-3 calls per week, many of which are just internal meetings aka extremely basic). With that, it doesn't make sense for us to have a stand-alone scheduling software.

BUT we'd recommend Cal.com over Motion for any business who has scheduling needs that are more robust, especially serviced based businesses or any business that does sales + customer support calls.
